name: ligature-melt
title: Ligature Melt
description: Headline whose glyphs liquefy near the cursor — an SVG gooey filter fuses neighbors into temporary ligatures that spring apart on leave.
instruction: A headline where characters near the cursor liquefy into temporary ligatures. One span per glyph inside a container carrying CSS filter: url(#goo); the inline SVG filter is feGaussianBlur stdDeviation 6 into an feColorMatrix with alpha row 0 0 0 19 -9 (blur + threshold), so overlapping glyph edges fuse into metaball necks. Text stays real DOM — selectable and SEO-safe, the filter is visual only. A Gaussian field (sigma 70px) around the cursor x scales affected glyphs to 1 + 0.35*g and translates them toward the cursor by up to 6px so edges overlap and goo; total line width stays constant by redistributing the induced width surplus as compression across out-of-field spans each frame with line start/end pinned. Per-span state (scale x/y, dx) lives in plain arrays written as transforms by a direct-DOM rAF loop — no React state on the hot path. Approach eases via lerp 0.15/frame; on pointer leave every span snaps back on an underdamped spring (k = 170 s^-2, zeta = 0.55) with visible surface-tension overshoot as the ligatures pinch apart. Loop sleeps when max delta < 0.002. Spans are measured once via offsetLeft/offsetWidth and remeasured on ResizeObserver. Under prefers-reduced-motion the filter is removed and the text renders static and crisp with no listeners. Zero dependencies.
